headline: Data Center Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill aims to shift the cost of grid infrastructure upgrades, driven by large energy users like data centers, from residential ratepayers to the corporations themselves.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Governor Spanberger's administration, consumer advocates, environmental advocates, some lawmakers.
news_headline: Virginia mulls shifting major grid costs to data centers
news_summary: Virginia regulators are considering how data center developers should bear more of the costs for transmission projects, which are currently spread across the public, with state residents having paid billions since 2021. Governor Spanberger and advocates argue data centers should pay for infrastructure driven by their demand, aiming to protect ratepayers from rising electricity bills.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates reporting on data center water consumption, particularly in water scarcity areas, and requires efforts to minimize water usage for cooling.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Governor Spanberger's administration, environmental groups, some lawmakers concerned about water resources.
opponents: Potentially data center industry due to increased regulatory burden.
news_headline: Virginia study on groundwater, data centers calls for tighter water regulations
news_summary: A Virginia study found declining groundwater availability in the eastern region due to population growth and industrial use, urging stricter regulations on water withdrawals. The report suggests regulators need more authority to reject permits and require alternative water sources, though it didn't blame data centers directly for aquifer concerns.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Rules
short_summary: This bill requires localities to consider noise and siting standards for data centers through their zoning ordinances and mandates noise studies for new facilities.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near data centers, environmental advocates, some lawmakers.
news_headline: Manassas Tightens Data Center Zoning Rules
news_summary: Manassas City Council approved a zoning ordinance to tighten development rules for data centers, addressing concerns about noise, appearance, and proximity to residential areas. The changes aim to reduce constant hum from cooling systems and backup generators, strengthen architectural design, and formalize requirements previously negotiated with developers.
